title: Recurring amount limits on the server, local-only QA account scripts, and duplicate protection for settle-up

acceptance_criteria.outcome: Recurring run-now and confirm accept only the normal money amount (over 0, at most 1,000,000, two decimals). Anything else, including NaN and Infinity, creates no expense and leaves the occurrence unprocessed; an omitted amount still uses the template's.
The QA account, verification and reset-token scripts connect only to a trackspense_qa or trackspense_e2e_* database on this machine, and refuse anything else before connecting.

A settlement sent with a request_id is stored once: sending it again returns the original, marked already_recorded, with no new row, activity or notification, also when two arrive together; the same id for a different payment is refused (409). Without an id nothing changes.

Web and mobile send a request_id with every recorded settlement and reuse it when the same payment (group, payer, payee, amount) is sent again within an hour after an unknown outcome, while the app stays open, including after a retry that fails offline, signed out or rate limited. Success or a 409 releases it, as does a refusal of a payment that was never unconfirmed. When the server answers already_recorded, the app says nothing new was added and that a second payment must be recorded again.
Settling one expense share locks the expense while the share is checked and recorded, so concurrent requests record at most one settlement.

A settled share stays marked as paid when its expense or its receipt items are edited (same or new amount), including edits that overlap a payment or each other, so it cannot be settled again; a changed amount shows in the balances. Deleting the payment makes the share settleable again.
When web or mobile is told a share was already settled (409), it says so and refreshes the balances; any other refusal leaves the expense open.
